newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate eases.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate eases.

text.p: The Thai baht was lower in late quiet trade on Wednesday in local market while offshore parties continued being kept out of trading activities, dealers said.
The baht eased to 25.830/25.860 to the dollar late in onshore market from 25.810/25.830 in early morning. But in offshore market, the baht firmed to 25.790/25.820 from 25.830/25.860 earlier.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.82 per dollar against 25.80 on Tuesday.
"The market was quiet as usual. This will continue until the central bank's measure is lifted," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The Bank of Thailand has imposed the the two-tier exchange rate system since the baht came under speculative attack in mid-May, dealers said.

Under the system aimed at staving off offshore attacks on the baht, the Bank of Thailand cut off baht supply for offshore players by asking Thai-based commercial banks not to lend baht to foreign buyers.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was traded at 13/18 satangs per dollar in onshore market and 34/45 satangs in offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 10.00-11.00 percent late from 11.50-12.00 percent in early morning, dealers said.
Dealers said any further sharp decline in interbank rates is unlikely due to corporate tax payment due from late this month.
They said about 40-50 billion baht of funds are expected to be drained out of the market to meet corporate tax requirement.
